questions.question: Describe how lines of latitude and longitude appear on a flat map and where their degrees are shown.
questions.expected_answer: Lines of latitude run across the map from left to right, and lines of longitude run up and down from top to bottom, sometimes curving towards the poles. The degrees of latitude are printed on the left and right edges, and the degrees of longitude along the top and bottom edges.

questions.question: List the steps for reading the position of a city on a map.
questions.expected_answer: Find the city. Read its latitude from the nearby lines of latitude, deciding whether it is north or south of the equator and estimating between lines. Read its longitude from the nearby lines of longitude, deciding whether it is east or west of Greenwich. Write latitude first, then longitude, with the directions.

questions.question: Thirty degrees north, thirty-one degrees east is Cairo, and thirty degrees south, thirty-one degrees east is Durban. What does this show?
questions.expected_answer: It shows that the direction letters are essential. The same numbers can describe two places thousands of kilometres apart, one north and one south of the equator, so a position must always say north or south and east or west.
